sections.title: Project Economics & the Permit Binary
sections.subtitle: Santana earns no revenue. Everything below is a claim on the Bendigo-Ophir project's PFS-modelled cash flows, contingent on one regulatory decision due 16 December 2026.

charts.title: Cash on Hand — the Funding Runway
charts.annotation: Balance-sheet cash only. Post the Feb-2026 A$134.1m raise, presented net cash is ~A$185m vs A$277m pre-production capex — a funding gap the base case closes with a further A$140m raise.

charts.title: Shares Outstanding — the Dilution Story
charts.annotation: Restated onto one consistent basis across a 1:70 consolidation (Oct-2020) and a 3:1 split (Oct-2024) — the jumps in the raw history are corporate actions, not errors. Fully-diluted count is now ~992.5m per the Aug-2026 presentation (986m FPO + 6.5m options), above the H1 FY2026 balance-sheet figure of 835.6m.

charts.title: Exploration & Development Investment
charts.annotation: Negative values are exploration and development spend, not distress — this is a pre-production developer investing in the PFS, not an operating company. Scales toward the A$277m pre-production capex once construction begins.

sections.title: Balance Sheet & Corporate Burn
sections.subtitle: What it has spent and what it holds, not how it is performing — there is no revenue to measure performance against.

charts.title: Shareholders' Equity vs Total Assets
charts.annotation: The asset build is almost entirely capitalised exploration spend (Exploration & Evaluation Asset A$71.1m at H1 FY2026) funded by equity issuance, not retained earnings — there has never been a profitable period.

charts.title: Net Income — Corporate Burn
charts.annotation: Every period is a loss — this is a pre-revenue developer, not an underperforming operator. FY2021's larger loss reflects a one-off; the underlying run-rate is corporate overhead plus non-capitalised exploration costs.

charts.title: Operating Cash Flow vs Free Cash Flow
charts.annotation: Negative FCF is the point, not a warning sign: it is exploration and development capital being deployed ahead of first gold (targeted 2028), funded by the cash and equity raises shown elsewhere on this page.

charts.title: Share-Based Compensation
charts.annotation: Small in absolute terms (A$0.1-0.7m/yr) relative to the equity raises funding the project — the real dilution driver is capital raising, charted separately in Shares Outstanding, not options/incentives.

cashRunway.title: Cash on Hand
cashRunway.content:
Balance-sheet cash and equivalents at each period end. For a pre-revenue developer this is the entire liquidity runway — there is no operating cash inflow to fall back on.

For Santana: cash grew to A$90.0m at 31-Dec-2025, then to a presented ~A$185m after the Feb-2026 A$130m institutional placement (A$0.90/share) plus a A$4.1m Share Purchase Plan — raised specifically to close the funding gap to the A$277m pre-production capex estimate.

What to watch:

  • Whether cash plus any project debt facility closes the full A$277m capex gap without further large dilutive raises
  • Burn rate between now and the Dec-2026 permit decision
  • Any lender technical due diligence outcome (Independent Technical Expert appointed, per company disclosures)

dilution.title: Shares Outstanding
dilution.content:
Total shares on issue, restated onto one consistent basis. Santana's history includes a 1:70 share consolidation (October 2020) and a 3:1 share split (October 2024) — both corporate actions, not data errors, and this series has been adjusted so the trend is comparable across them.

For Santana: share count has grown roughly 40x since FY2019 (23m to ~992.5m fully diluted) purely through equity issuance to fund exploration, the PFS and now development readiness — there has never been a buyback.

What to watch:

  • The size and pricing of the next raise needed to close the A$277m capex gap (base case models a further A$140m at A$0.70/share)
  • Whether project debt substitutes for some of the equity need (the bull case assumes A$100m of debt)
  • Dilution is the single biggest swing factor between the base and bull per-share valuations

capex.title: Exploration & Development Investment
capex.content:
Cash spent on exploration, evaluation and project development — the CSV's CapEx line. Because Santana has no revenue, this is investment ahead of production, not maintenance spend on an existing asset base.

For Santana: spend has scaled from under A$1m/yr in the early exploration phase to over A$20m in H1 FY2026 alone as the project moves from resource definition through PFS to early site works (raw water pipeline, access upgrades) ahead of a construction decision.

What to watch:

  • Step-up to the full A$277m pre-production capital programme once (if) consent is granted
  • Cost inflation against the PFS's 10% contingency and ±15% accuracy band

equityBuild.title: Shareholders' Equity vs Total Assets
equityBuild.content:
Book equity and total assets from the balance sheet. For a pre-revenue developer these grow almost entirely through capitalised exploration spend funded by new equity, not through retained profit.

For Santana: the Exploration & Evaluation Asset alone was A$71.1m at H1 FY2026, up from A$5.6m in FY2016 — the balance sheet is a running record of capital raised and deployed into the project, not a measure of operating performance.

What to watch:

  • Whether book value bears any relationship to the PFS-derived project NPV (A$780m-A$1.52bn) once risk-adjusted for the permit decision
  • A negative permit outcome would likely require material impairment of the capitalised exploration asset

burn.title: Net Income — Corporate Burn
burn.content:
Statutory net income/loss each period. Every historical period is negative — this chart exists to show the scale and trend of the burn, not to imply an underperforming operating business, because there is no operating business yet.

For Santana: losses have generally scaled with company size and activity level (corporate overhead, non-capitalised study and consulting costs) rather than signalling deteriorating unit economics, since there are no units being sold.

What to watch:

  • The burn rate relative to cash on hand as the funding runway to first gold (2028 target)
  • Any one-off items (e.g. the larger FY2021 loss) that distort period-on-period comparisons

fcf.title: Operating Cash Flow vs Free Cash Flow
fcf.content:
Cash generated (or consumed) by operations, and free cash flow after capital expenditure. For Santana both are structurally negative and that is expected, not a warning sign: this is investment capital being deployed into a pre-production project, not cash leaking out of a struggling operating business.

For Santana: FCF has grown more negative each year (from roughly -A$2.9m in FY2018 to -A$16.3m in FY2025 and -A$20.4m in H1 FY2026 alone) as the project has moved from early exploration through the PFS into development readiness — funded entirely by the cash and equity raises shown in the other charts on this page.

What to watch:

  • The step-up to full construction-phase capex (A$277m) once (if) the permit is granted
  • Cash and financing (equity/debt) staying ahead of the burn

sbc.title: Share-Based Compensation
sbc.content:
Non-cash equity compensation expensed to management, directors and staff. Small in absolute dollar terms for Santana relative to the capital raises that actually drive dilution.

For Santana: SBC has run at roughly A$0.1-0.7m/yr — immaterial next to the tens/hundreds of millions raised in primary equity issuance, which is why the DCF's SBC-adjustment band collapses to a single number rather than a house/street range.

What to watch:

  • Any step-up in SBC as the company scales toward construction and hires an operating team

dcf.growth_hint: Not a growth-DCF — disabled; this is a risked project-NPV (sum-of-parts) model on the permit outcome, not a revenue growth projection
dcf.base_sublabel: Risked project-NPV (sum-of-parts): P(permit) × project NPV + net cash + raise proceeds − dilution − overhead. No owner-FCF projection exists to discount.
